scores.why: Ten sheets meet the limit, but repeated explanations slow the presentation and sheet 9 contains approximately 756 words outside collapsed details.

fixes.change: Keep the proposition, A/B choice, channel table and decision request visible; move the expanded insight, tone and readiness recap into details.

fixes.quote: The same three contradictions from sheet 05, now each with a person’s decision.
fixes.change: Remove this takeaway: the title, margin and three resolution blocks already communicate it.

fixes.quote: The budget stays «κάπου στα ογδόντα»: no invented or resolved total in the brief or either render. Shadow Draft A invented one; the creative lead strikes it.
fixes.change: Remove this repeated campaign-budget recap from the pilot decision sheet.

scores.why: The evidence, deliverables, usage, timings and human responsibilities are covered, but the CFO still lacks an assigned action to price the pilot and its ongoing support.

fixes.quote: Pilot effort and operating costs are still to be estimated.
fixes.change: Turn this ledger caveat into a visible decision action: management and the operator estimate setup, training, subscription and maintenance effort before pilot spending is approved.

fixes.quote: Second fixture: 15/17, then 16/17 after a re-roll; exam-green is not lead-ready.
fixes.change: Add the concrete consequence from the cited report: the second fixture retained a superseded launch date despite passing the conflict check, so reviewers must verify meaning as well as citations.

scores.why: The AI/code/people distinction is strong, but technical terminology and compressed metric labels still make the CMO work harder than necessary.

fixes.quote: The account lead writes each resolution into brief.json (conflicts[n].resolution, resolved_by) and the sign-off block (status, signed_by, signed_ts, edits_summary): a schema-validated edit in v1, a one-page runbook by week 1 (PRD §8).
fixes.change: Use plain language in the margin: the lead manually records decisions and approval in the master file using a runbook; put field names and validation mechanics in the ledger.

fixes.quote: Targets: question precision >80%, draft survival >70%, review <30 minutes; Greek-language quality and voluntary adoption.
fixes.change: Explain the measures here: over 80% of questions judged useful, over 70% of draft text retained, and under 30 minutes reviewing.

scores.why: The answer-first opening and evidence-to-decision sequence work, but the creative takeaway is convoluted and the closing title promises more certainty than its actions establish.

fixes.quote: The creative drafts stayed inside the signed-off facts and the spec table, except three things to strike and one call for the creative lead.
fixes.change: Replace with a direct takeaway: “The shadow drafts need three corrections and a creative lead’s decision.”

fixes.quote: Approve the four-week pilot: usage is measured in tokens, the cost of running it is not yet, and week 1 settles both.
fixes.change: Replace with “Approve a conditional pilot; confirm capacity and operating effort before it starts,” matching the stated pre-week-1 actions.

scores.why: Brief Builder has a clear identity, anatomy, outputs and operating boundaries, but its business promise and everyday workflow receive less prominence than its implementation.

fixes.change: Move the code-size and agent-count explanation into the ledger and use this margin for the daily workflow: assemble files, operator runs, lead reviews and records approval, creative lead evaluates.

fixes.quote: Brief Builder turns a client’s pile of documents into a Greek and English brief.
fixes.change: Add the business purpose immediately: more consistent briefs across account leads, with reduced preparation time as a pilot target.

scores.why: The source defines a coherent editorial system with restrained colour and clear role markings, although long headings and the small mobile portrait treatment weaken hierarchy.

fixes.quote: Nine steps, three roles: six are AI, two are plain code, and the one that releases the work is a person.
fixes.change: Shorten the heading to “AI drafts, code checks, and a person releases the work”; let the numbered diagram carry the step count.
At phone widths, enlarge the portrait plate beyond the current 56% width so its wordmark and mock-up label remain comfortably readable.

scores.why: Headline totals, model IDs, timings and the 17 checks match the artifacts, but two smaller statements need correction or clearer attribution.

fixes.quote: Clear space of one wordmark height kept free on every side of the name; ring, leaf and name sit in the central column so the 9:16 crop clips nothing
fixes.change: Replace the stale ring-and-leaf description with the actual wind stroke and bubbles, and limit the clear-space assertion to applications that have been checked.
Label week 1 as a proposed earlier deadline; PRD §8 specifies champion training on the runbook by week 4.

scores.why: Offline assets, keyboard controls, focus handling and return navigation are implemented, but mobile CSS crowds the contents control and places crucial creative warnings after the entire sheet.

fixes.change: Keep Contents outside the horizontally scrolling tick strip, or hide ticks on phones; ten minimum-width ticks currently compete with a contents button allowed to shrink nearly to its padding.
Place the “Three strikes, one call” warning directly before the creative draft on small screens instead of after the long body.

scores.why: The wind-and-fizz artwork and can make the output tangible with honest mock-up labels, but the can breaches wordmark clearance and the portrait crop knowingly leaves the lockup in the caption zone.

fixes.change: Increase separation above and below the can’s wordmark to at least one wordmark height; the inspected image places both the yellow mark and category line too close.

fixes.quote: 9:16 still frame at the TikTok in-feed spec; the lockup sits in TikTok’s caption zone, a dedicated 9:16 layout would raise it
fixes.change: Show the dedicated portrait layout with the lockup raised, retaining the provisional-spec and illustration labels.

overall: A credible, evidence-rich pilot case that needs tighter presentation and mobile/creative refinement before shipping unchanged. The required SHA-256 matched before and after review; no repository files were changed. Chrome failed to launch, so layout and navigation scores are based on source inspection, supplemented by direct inspection of the embedded can image.
